text:
maria: quick sync — I'm proposing we simplify the operator API for warmup credits. current shape ties credits to reservation tokens and the admission flow is messy.
sam: can you sketch the pain points?
maria: sure. main issues: 1) operator has to call into runtime to deduct credits during admit, which blocks operator retries, 2) credits leak when pods restart, 3) metrics are scattered between operator/runtime so alerting is noisy.
kevin: yeah we've seen leaks in prod during rolling restarts. spikes in warmup usage but metrics drop to zero mid-rollout.
raj: to be concrete, what's the new API idea?
maria: decouple warmup-credit accounting from reservation tokens. operator will emit a short-lived claim (opaque id) and runtime will periodically poll the claims endpoint. operator is authoritative for intent; runtime consumes claims asynchronously and reconciles local cache.
sam: async is safer for operator liveness, but what about double-spend? two runtimes consuming same claim?
kevin: make claim deletion idempotent and provide a TTL. runtime does compare-and-delete with an api like `POST /claims/consume` returning either `consumed` or `already_taken`.
raj: must preserve billing/chargeback accuracy though.
maria: billing will be driven from reconciliation logs — operator writes canonical events to the ledger (eventually consistent). runtime consumption just marks local prewarm usage; final billing is reconciled by operator.
sam: any changes to admission latency? we don't want a blocking RPC in the hotpath.
maria: non-blocking for admit. admit only checks operator intent label, falls back to cold path if no local prewarm. runtime best-effort pulls claims and prepopulates caches.
kevin: rollout plan? how do we avoid cold starts for tenants that still on old flow?
maria: hybrid compatibility: operator will expose both v1 (token-based) and v2 (claim-based). runtime reads v2 when available; fallbacks look for v1. Gradual migration via feature flags per fleet.
raj: sounds reasonable. What about observability? i want a single metric for active prewarm credits and a counter for `claims_consumed`.
maria: plan: operator-exported metrics: `operator_prewarm_claims_total`, `operator_prewarm_claims_active`, runtime-exported: `runtime_local_prewarm_cache_hits`, `runtime_claims_consumed_total`. We'll add a reconciliation job that emits `prewarm_billing_delta`.
sam: edge cases: operator crash during claim creation -> orphaned claims. TTL solves that; also add periodic garbage collection that reclaims expired claims.
kevin: what about security — tenant isolation for claims? anyone can create claims currently in our cluster.
maria: claims namespace will be scoped per-tenant, require tenant label, and operator signs claim ids with HMAC so runtime verifies signature before consuming.
raj: example API surface? small sketch?
maria: posted below:
```
POST /claims {
  tenant: "acme",
  claim_id: "c_123",
  credits: 5,
  expires_at: 1718209000,
  sig: "hmac..."
}
POST /claims/consume { claim_id: "c_123", sig: "hmac..." } -> { status: "consumed" }
GET /claims?tenant=acme -> list active (for operator debug)
```
sam: lgtm. HMAC key rotation? store in k8s secret with version, operator includes version in claim.
kevin: tests we need: chaos test with operator restart, runtime consumer double-try, GC test.
maria: will add unit tests + integration harness that simulates 100 tenants with churn. propose we run in canary fleet for 2 days.
raj: rollout phasing: 1) implement v2 endpoints + feature flag, 2) runtime reads v2 opt-in, 3) migrate a small set of tenants, 4) monitor reconciliation metrics, 5) flip default.
sam: any perf numbers expected? how often should runtime poll claims endpoint?
maria: start with 5s poll, can tune. expectation: steady-state extra api calls per runtime ~ 12/min per tenant herd, negligible vs other control plane traffic.
kevin: I'll help with the operator GC implementation.
maria: thanks — I'll write up a short RFC follow-up with the API sketch and rollout steps. tagging for visibility: @sam @kevin @raj
devops-bot: deploy pipeline check: `ci/operator` passed, `ci/runtime` pending.
maria: awesome :thumbsup: I'll post the RFC link once it's up.
